about: Sad Pablo Escobar is a three-shot collage of Wagner Moura as Pablo Escobar from Narcos, each frame a portrait of lonely waiting. In the top shot he sits on a swing bench in a short-sleeved blue shirt, staring at nothing. Below left, he slumps at a cheap kitchen table in a dim room; below right, he stands alone at the edge of a drained, empty swimming pool, hands behind his back. Strung together, the shots tell a story of someone hoping for something that is never going to arrive. People caption it with whatever they are waiting on in vain: a reply, a delivery, a friend who said they were on their way.
origin: The stills are from the Netflix series Narcos, from its second season released in 2016, which follows the final period of drug lord Pablo Escobar's life. The scenes show him isolated while in hiding.
usage:
The top box sets up the wait, usually starting with "me waiting for..." or "when you...". The bottom box names the thing that never comes, often stretched out as the punchline: "to laugh at my meme", "for the bus that was 2 minutes away 20 minutes ago".

It fits unanswered texts, game updates, sequels that never got made, slow customer support, parties nobody showed up to and players waiting for teammates to load in. The three empty scenes make it best for loneliness that is funny rather than truly sad.
